experiment: Scan callee names without temporary identifier nodes
hypothesis: Collecting callee names directly removes temporary EIdent construction and a recursive scan; reads, calls and assignment targets share the same binding judgment.
correctness_counterexamples: First-occurrence order and deduplication across reads/calls/writes
Inner and enclosing bindings preceding global names
Inline builtin call skipping versus ordinary identifier references
Throw payload-only scan versus general perform callees

callee_extra_heap_growth_bytes.comparison: direct call minus bare identifier; AST construction excluded
callee_extra_heap_growth_bytes.note: The two entries are local-bound and global callees. RC can reuse the first temporary block on the next query; its heap-pointer delta is not total allocation volume.

aa.cache: new process per sample; empty cache for cold, same populated cache for warm; OS cache uncontrolled
aa.compiler_memory_mode: determined by supplied binaries, not inferred from names or VIBE_RC

bump.compiler_memory_mode: determined by supplied binaries, not inferred from names or VIBE_RC

profiles.note: Separate diagnostic runs, not uninstrumented wall-time samples; both compilers read the final source snapshot.

interpretation: The comparison is a pure compiler implementation change: every generated target is byte-identical across compilers, temperatures and rounds. Heap-pointer, linear capacity and RSS are distinct metrics. Wall-time spread and the A/A control limit the precision of timing claims.
